title: CAT 2021 Question Paper (Slot 1, PYQ) - Quantitative Ability - Numbers
subject: Quantitative Ability

questions.q: How many three-digit numbers are greater than 100 and increase by 198 when the three digits are arranged in the reverse order?
questions.explain:
Let the original 3-digit number be $N = 100a + 10b + c$, where $a \ge 1$ (since it's a 3-digit number > 100). 
Reversed number $M = 100c + 10b + a$.
Given $M - N = 198 \implies (100c + 10b + a) - (100a + 10b + c) = 198$.
$99(c - a) = 198 \implies c - a = 2$.
Since $a$ is the leading digit of the original number, $a$ can range from 1 to 7 (because $c$ can at most be 9, so $a = c-2 \le 7$).
For each valid $a$ (1 to 7), $c$ is fixed as $a+2$.
The middle digit $b$ can be any digit from 0 to 9. So there are 10 choices for $b$ for every $(a, c)$ pair.
Total possible numbers = 7 (pairs of $a,c$) $\times$ 10 (choices for $b$) = 70.
